pr.title: Mark items done and switch between open, done and all

acceptance.evidence: migrations/0002_add_done.sql adds done NOT NULL DEFAULT 0; test/done.test.js 'AC-1' checks existing rows are 0 and the CHECK rejects 2.
'AC-2' test checks / and ?view=open list only open items in id order.
'AC-3' test marks 3,1 done and expects ['✓ First item','✓ Third item'] in order.
'AC-4' test expects all three in id order with only the done one marked.
'AC-5' asserts the exact nav HTML for each view and for /.
'AC-6' checks 400 and no <li> for Open, closed, empty and __proto__; Object.hasOwn guards the lookup.

The 'AC-7' test and the 'Empty table', 'Nothing open' and 'Nothing done' state tests really check the messages. The spec's new 'verified by review: checked by hand' mark is not a real step, but the tests make the item met. The late edit to this item is a separate high finding.
traffic/routes.json lists both views; the 'AC-8' test checks them.

findings.what: Commit fa75889 ('Follow-up edits', by a bot) edited acceptance item AC-7 after the go (2026-10-12). It appended 'verified by review: checked by hand', which is not a followable step. It also left the sentence reading oddly ('a view with nothing in it — verified by review: checked by hand says ...'). No decision in the spec records an owner call or date for this edit.
findings.fix: Revert the AC-7 edit. The tests already prove the item. If the wording really needs to change, record the owner's decision and date in the spec.

findings.what: The PR says 'Changed after the go: nothing', but the final commit changed AC-7 in the spec after the go.
findings.fix: Revert the edit, or state the change in the PR and record the owner's approval.

findings.what: The README doesn't mention that unknown view values answer 400, or the new migration.
findings.fix: Add a short note on the 400 for an unknown view.

lenses.note: A spec exists, and its go is dated 2026-10-12.
All eight items have tests that name them, and each row of the state table has a test. The late commit edits AC-7.
The tests assert behaviour and would fail if the code were wrong. I did not run them, because the Cloudflare vitest pool may not be available here. CI runs them.
The README covers the views. It's missing the 400 behaviour.
The view lookup uses Object.hasOwn, so there's no prototype issue. The SQL fragments are constants, not user input. The empty-table check costs an extra query only when a view is empty.
The view parameter is whitelisted and titles are escaped. The traffic regex change still refuses spaces and '#'. No planted instructions found.
The diff touches no CSS or frontend files. It has only server-rendered HTML in src/index.js.
There's no browser flow to run here. The page is plain server-rendered HTML, and the tests cover it.
The claim 'Changed after the go: nothing' is false, because the final commit edited AC-7.
